title: Chest Radiograph: Air Bronchogram and Silhouette Sign
subject: Radiological Signs
preview: An air bronchogram appears when air-filled bronchi are outlined by surrounding opaque alveolar lung.
quickRevision: An air bronchogram appears when air-filled bronchi are outlined by surrounding opaque alveolar lung.
Consolidation, edema and other air-space processes may produce air bronchograms; the finding is not pathogen-specific.
Evaluate radiograph projection, rotation and clinical context before assigning a lobe or diagnosis.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: An air bronchogram appears when air-filled bronchi are outlined by surrounding opaque alveolar lung.
The silhouette sign localizes disease by loss of a normal border between structures of similar density.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Consolidation, edema and other air-space processes may produce air bronchograms; the finding is not pathogen-specific.
Evaluate radiograph projection, rotation and clinical context before assigning a lobe or diagnosis.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: An air bronchogram does not alone distinguish bacterial from viral pneumonia.

quiz.question: Why does an air bronchogram become visible?
options: Air in bronchi contrasts with surrounding opaque alveoli
quiz.explanation: Air in bronchi contrasts with surrounding opaque alveoli. An air bronchogram appears when air-filled bronchi are outlined by surrounding opaque alveolar lung.
